method: Agent-enumerated from domain knowledge of DeFi governance, wallet provider, app-store, and RPC-provider censorship events 2017-2025. Each candidate verified via WebSearch against contemporaneous reporting (CoinDesk, Decrypt, The Block, Cointelegraph, Fortune, CryptoSlate, etc.) and, where available, first-party corporate / regulator pages. No automated scraper used.
cross_check_method: Each candidate slug cross-checked against the 122 admitted event ids in events/*.yaml and the 21 promoted_event_id values in candidate_triggers/. Verified events already in corpus for this frame: uniswap-frontend-delisting-2023 (S5 L4-only DEX delisting), infura-alchemy-tornado-rpc-block-2022 (S5 L3 RPC sanctions block), tornado-cash-ofac-2022 (S1 OFAC trigger with cross-layer cascade observations), circle-usdc-tornado-2022 (asset_onchain sibling), tornado-cash-ofac-delisting-2025 (recovery), sec-v-uniswap-wells-notice-2024 (S3 SEC frontend enforcement), canada-convoy-freeze-2022 (offramp_cex Emergencies-Act freeze).
exclusion_notes: Aave/Uniswap/Balancer August-2022 frontend Tornado-Cash interaction blocks are documented downstream of the OFAC trigger event tornado-cash-ofac-2022; that event's observations[l4_frontend] partially covers this cascade. Each protocol's frontend action is enumerated here as a separate S5_corporate candidate because the individual protocol-frontend decisions are independent corporate policy changes (TRM API integration, IPFS frontend updates) that should be measured separately from the OFAC trigger; if the schema treats them as already-subsumed by tornado-cash-ofac-2022 observations[l4_frontend], fold them in rather than admit.

Apple App Store removal of nine offshore exchanges from India (2024-01-10) and Google Play removal of same set (2024-01-14) are downstream of the india-fiu-offshore-vda-block-2023 trigger already in corpus. Enumerated here as separate L4 candidates because the app-store removals are corporate-policy actions by Apple/Google distinct from the FIU notice itself; they constitute the first major app-store-layer crypto censorship cascade observable globally.

MetaMask/Infura 2022-03-03 Venezuela block was a self-described accidental over-broad enforcement of the 2022-02 Donetsk/Luhansk sanctions and was reversed within days; it remains valuable as a P1 case study of L3/L4 over-blocking risk and the IP-geo enforcement mechanism, even though the corporate action was rapidly walked back.

Trust Wallet, Rabby, Frame, WalletConnect did not surface concrete public dated policy-change events in this round of WebSearch beyond ToS-level boilerplate; none enumerated. Lido, Compound, Curve, SushiSwap governance/frontend events are present in the literature but the specific dated decisions are either pre-existing (Compound pause Proposal 131 is a risk-management action not a censorship event) or insufficiently anchored to a single trigger date.
Coinbase Wallet, Phantom wallet scam-token blocklists are user-protection actions (not government-driven censorship); not enumerated.
ConsenSys / MetaMask Snaps regional restrictions and other ongoing ToS updates are policy-class triggers without a single trigger date; not enumerated.

Polymarket CFTC settlement 2022-01-03 is a US federal enforcement (S3) action; could be re-framed as offramp-class. Enumerated here as P0 because the geofence implementation against US users is the load-bearing L4 cascade and is the cleanest prediction-market-platform-level L4 block in the corpus.

candidates.title: Infura/MetaMask Venezuela accidental block while implementing Donetsk/Luhansk sanctions (ConsenSys)
candidates.rationale: First documented L3 RPC-provider IP-geo block of sanctioned regions: ConsenSys Infura implemented OFAC-compliance geoblocks against the Donetsk/Luhansk separatist regions (per 2022-02-21 EO 14065) and accidentally over-blocked Venezuela, Iran, and other jurisdictions on 2022-03-03. Triggers the L3/L4 cascade observable through MetaMask, which used Infura as default RPC. Cleanest pre-Tornado-Cash L3 RPC sanctions-screening event in the corpus; structurally distinct from infura-alchemy-tornado-rpc-block-2022 (address-set screening vs IP-geo region screening). Paper-relevant: documents the IP-geo mechanism of L3 enforcement vs the address-set mechanism.

candidates.title: OpenSea blocks Iranian and Cuban users / artists (NFT marketplace IP-geo + nationality screening)
candidates.rationale: OpenSea (the dominant NFT marketplace frontend) deactivated/deleted Iranian-user accounts 2022-03-03 citing OFAC compliance; subsequently extended ban to Cuban artists in December 2022, including Cuban-passport holders living outside Cuba. CEO Devin Finzer publicly confirmed IP-address screening against OFAC sanctions list. Cleanest L4 corporate frontend nationality-screening event in the corpus; structurally adjacent to uniswap-frontend-delisting-2023 (token-level frontend filtering) but with the orthogonal axis of user/nationality-level frontend filtering. Strong paper-relevance for the L4 column.

candidates.title: Aave frontend (app.aave.com / IPFS frontend) block of Tornado-Cash-tainted addresses via TRM API
candidates.rationale: Aave integrated TRM Labs' compliance API into its IPFS-served frontend within ~5 days of the 2022-08-08 OFAC Tornado Cash designation, blocking >600 wallets that had received Tornado-tainted ETH (including high-profile false-positive Justin Sun dust attack). Aave Companies publicly stated that on-chain (smart-contract-level) wallet screening would require an AIP / DAO vote — making this a frontend-only corporate action while the protocol remained unrestricted. Cleanest individual-DeFi-protocol L4 frontend Tornado-cascade event distinct from uniswap-frontend-delisting-2023 (no Tornado tie) and tornado-cash-ofac-2022 observations[l4_frontend] (which aggregates the cascade). Strong L4 column anchor.

candidates.title: Uniswap Labs and Balancer Labs frontend blocks of Tornado-Cash-tainted addresses (TRM/Chainalysis API integration)
candidates.rationale: Within ~4 days of the 2022-08-08 OFAC Tornado Cash designation, Uniswap Labs (app.uniswap.org) and Balancer Labs (app.balancer.fi) independently integrated compliance APIs (TRM Labs and Chainalysis) into their hosted frontends to block addresses tainted by Tornado Cash interactions. Balancer publicly confirmed that 'addresses' but 'nothing else' would be sent to authorities. Distinct from aave-tornado-frontend-block-2022-08 because the operator and the specific compliance-API integration differ. Together with the Aave row, this gives the corpus three independent L4 corporate frontend Tornado-Cash cascade observations from the same 2022-08-08 trigger.

candidates.title: Apple App Store removes nine offshore crypto exchange apps from India (Binance, KuCoin, OKX, Kraken, Gate.io, Bittrex, Bitstamp, MEXC, Bitfinex)
candidates.rationale: First major app-store-layer crypto censorship cascade observable in the corpus. Apple removed nine offshore VASP apps from the India App Store on 2024-01-10, ~13 days after India's FIU 2023-12-28 show-cause notices (covered separately by india-fiu-offshore-vda-block-2023). Corporate-policy action by Apple distinct from the regulator trigger; structurally the same as a frontend-operator delisting except the operator is the platform-distribution layer. Load-bearing L4 anchor: the iOS App Store is the dominant distribution channel for mobile crypto-app users globally, and this is the first documented full-platform crypto-exchange-app removal at app-store level driven by FIU/regulator pressure.

candidates.title: Google Play Store removes Binance, KuCoin, OKX and other offshore crypto exchange apps from India
candidates.rationale: Google Play removed offshore VASP apps from India 4 days after the Apple App Store action (apple-india-crypto-exchange-removal-2024-01). Same underlying FIU trigger, different platform-distribution actor; the staggered timing is itself paper-relevant as evidence of independent corporate-compliance decision-making across Apple/Google. Pairs structurally with the Apple row to anchor the 'two app-store gatekeeper' L4 column observation.

candidates.title: Polymarket CFTC settlement + US geofence implementation (prediction-market platform)
candidates.rationale: CFTC settled with Polymarket 2022-01-03 for $1.4M civil penalty for operating an unregistered DCM/SEF; settlement required Polymarket to wind down non-compliant markets and bar US users. Polymarket implemented IP-based geo-blocking against US users immediately after settlement. Distinct from cftc-v-ooki-dao-2022 (DAO enforcement) and sec-v-coinbase-2023 (CEX enforcement) because the target is a frontend prediction-market platform and the cascade is L4-frontend-only (IP geofencing). Cleanest 2022 federal-enforcement-to-L4-geofence cascade. The geofence's documented circumvention via VPN (e.g., 2024 soldier $400K classified-info trades) makes this a paper-relevant case study of L4 effectiveness.

candidates.title: 1inch DEX aggregator implements US-user geofence ahead of 1inch Pro launch
candidates.rationale: 1inch Labs added a frontend pop-up + IP-geo technical layer on 2021-09-29 to block US users from app.1inch.io, citing pending 1inch Pro US-compliant launch. Predates the Uniswap July-2021 token-list curation and the August-2022 Tornado-driven L4 cascade; codes the first DEX-aggregator-level frontend geofence in the corpus. Structurally distinct from uniswap-frontend-delisting-2023 (token-level filtering) and opensea-iran-cuba-sanctions-block-2022 (nationality-level filtering) — 1inch is jurisdiction-level (US) for a non-sanctioned country. Important L4 column anchor for the 'voluntary jurisdiction geofence' subtype distinct from OFAC-mandated screening.

candidates.title: Uniswap Labs frontend removal of ~129 tokens including tokenized stocks, options, synthetic-derivative tokens
candidates.rationale: Uniswap Labs removed ~129 tokens (Synthetix mAssets, UMA, Opyn options, Tether Gold, Mirror tokenized stocks) from app.uniswap.org frontend on 2021-07-23, citing 'evolving regulatory landscape' (i.e., anticipated SEC scrutiny over tokenized securities). Predates the 2023-07-21 uniswap-frontend-delisting-2023 event already in corpus by 2 years — same operator, same mechanism (frontend-only filtering, protocol unaffected), different token universe (securities-flagged tokens vs OFAC/regulatory-flagged tokens). Cleanest first-instance L4 frontend-delisting precedent for the Uniswap operator; would strengthen the longitudinal L4 column.

candidates.title: Aave Arc permissioned-DeFi launch with Fireblocks as sole whitelister (30 institutional addresses)
candidates.rationale: Aave Arc went live 2022-01-05 as a permissioned fork of Aave V2 restricted to 30 institutional whitelisted addresses via Fireblocks' KYC framework. Cleanest example of governance-by-whitelist as a censorship architecture: address-level binary access control at the protocol layer, not a frontend filter. Distinct from L4 frontend events because the restriction is at the smart-contract level (whitelisting). Important paper-relevance for the 'governance-architecture-as-censorship' subtype; pairs with cftc-v-ooki-dao-2022 (already in corpus) to anchor the governance/DAO column.

candidates.title: Pump.fun blocks UK users following FCA Section 21 Section warning (memecoin platform geofence)
candidates.rationale: Pump.fun (Solana-based memecoin launchpad) implemented permanent UK-user geofence 2024-12-06, three days after UK FCA published an unauthorized-firm warning (2024-12-03). First documented memecoin-platform L4 geofence in the corpus; cleanest 2024 example of a non-US-non-OFAC frontend block driven by a non-US regulator (UK FCA). Trigger-actor is the operator (S5), proximate cause is the FCA warning (S2-equivalent). Strong L4 column anchor for the 'small-regulator-induced-frontend-block' subtype.

candidates.title: Augur V2 launches with US/UK geofence (Forecast Foundation prediction-market frontend)
candidates.rationale: Augur V2 (Forecast Foundation) launched 2020-07-28 with explicit US/UK/sanctioned-country frontend geofence, citing CFTC binary-options jurisdiction risk (the CFTC had publicly noted Augur contracts resemble binary options in July 2018). Cleanest pre-Polymarket L4 prediction-market geofence in the corpus; predates polymarket-cftc-geofence-2022-01 by 18 months. needs_check: confirmation of exact launch date on Forecast Foundation primary source. Important for L4 column longitudinal coverage of prediction-market geofencing.

candidates.title: Cloudflare Ethereum/IPFS gateway disables Tornado Cash sanctioned addresses
candidates.rationale: Cloudflare disabled access through its Ethereum Gateway and IPFS Gateway to the OFAC-designated Tornado Cash addresses/repositories within days of the 2022-08-08 sanctions. Distinct from infura-alchemy-tornado-rpc-block-2022 (managed Ethereum-RPC providers) because Cloudflare operates a public gateway / CDN, not a managed-RPC service; the censorship vector is the HTTP/IPFS access layer rather than the JSON-RPC layer. Cleanest documented L3-adjacent CDN-layer crypto sanctions block in the corpus. Strong paper-relevance for the L3 column's 'gateway/CDN' subtype distinct from the 'managed-RPC' subtype.

candidates.title: dYdX blocks accounts that received Tornado-Cash-tainted ETH (including innocent-dusted users)
candidates.rationale: dYdX (perpetuals DEX with off-chain order book + StarkEx L2) blocked accounts that had received ANY Tornado-tainted ETH on 2022-08-11, including users dust-attacked with small amounts. dYdX later partially unblocked some accounts and acknowledged the over-broad enforcement. Structurally similar to aave-tornado-frontend-block-2022-08 but with a stronger off-chain-order-book operator dimension (dYdX V3 ran on StarkEx with centralized matching). Distinct from polymarket-cftc-geofence because the trigger is OFAC-cascade not direct enforcement.

candidates.title: ConsenSys updates MetaMask/Infura privacy policy to collect user IP + Ethereum addresses on transactions
candidates.rationale: ConsenSys revised privacy policy 2022-11-23 confirming Infura logs MetaMask users' IP + Ethereum wallet addresses on every 'write' transaction. Not a direct block, but the surveillance infrastructure that enables L3 RPC sanctions screening — a paper-relevant precondition row. ConsenSys reverted some details after backlash (December 2022 MetaMask update plan). Codes the L3 'surveillance precondition' layer behind infura-alchemy-tornado-rpc-block-2022. Useful for the paper's claim about L3 substrate observability.

candidates.title: GitHub removes Tornado Cash repositories and developer accounts (Microsoft-owned source-hosting layer)
candidates.rationale: GitHub (Microsoft-owned) removed all known Tornado Cash repositories and developer accounts within hours of the 2022-08-08 OFAC SDN designation. Distinct from the L3 RPC block (infura-alchemy-tornado-rpc-block-2022) and L4 frontend cascade (tornado-cash-ofac-2022 observations) — this is the *source-code-distribution* layer block. A professor (Matthew Green, Johns Hopkins) republished code in protest; EFF litigation reference. First documented source-hosting takedown of sanctioned open-source crypto code; structurally adjacent to L4 frontend events but at the development-substrate layer.

candidates.title: MakerDAO governance contingency plan / 'free-floating DAI' debate following USDC Tornado freezes
candidates.rationale: MakerDAO Discord/forum debate August 2022 in which founder Rune Christensen disclosed governance-level contingency plans for an 'emergency shutdown' of DAI if Maker core contracts were sanctioned, and proposed depegging DAI from USDC. Predicate for the 2022-09 'Endgame' plan and the 2024-08 'Sky' rebrand. Codes the 'governance-policy-response-to-asset-layer-freeze' event downstream of circle-usdc-tornado-2022. Strong governance-column anchor for asset_onchain → governance feedback loop documented in the literature.

candidates.title: Ren Protocol 1.0 winds down following Alameda Research collapse (cross-chain bridge shutdown)
candidates.rationale: Ren Protocol 1.0 (cross-chain bridge for renBTC, renFIL, etc.) disabled minting November 2022 and ceased burning 2022-12-20 after Alameda Research funding (which kept the protocol's centralized dark-nodes operating) collapsed in FTX bankruptcy. Codes a 'collateral censorship via funder collapse' subtype — Alameda's failure operationally censored a major Bitcoin-to-Ethereum bridge for ~100,000 BTC users. Distinct from ftx-bankman-fried-doj-2022 (federal enforcement against FTX/Alameda) and asset-freeze events because the censorship is the bridge operator's shutdown action. Useful for the 'centralized dependency' L4/asset-onchain column.

candidates.title: Oasis.app court-ordered counter-exploit of Wormhole hacker (UK High Court instructs proxy upgrade)
candidates.rationale: UK High Court of England and Wales 2023-02-21 ordered Oasis.app to use its upgradeable proxy contract on Maker vaults to recover $140M of Wormhole-stolen funds from a third-party (the Wormhole exploiter). Codes a 'court-ordered governance-level asset transfer' event — DeFi platform compelled by a national court to seize funds via privileged smart-contract administration. First documented common-law-court-ordered DeFi protocol seizure in the corpus; strong paper-relevance for the 'governance-as-censorship' / 'admin-key-as-backdoor' subtype. Asset_onchain layer anchor.

candidates.title: Curve Finance frontend DNS hijack (.fi domain registrar / nameserver takeover)
candidates.rationale: Curve Finance frontend (curve.fi) DNS hijack May 2024 redirected users to a malicious clone via registrar/nameserver compromise. Not a direct censorship action by a state or corporate compliance team — included as P2 because the event documents the L4 frontend's DNS-substrate fragility (the DNS layer is itself a censorship-vector for any state with registrar jurisdiction). Useful only as a 'collateral L4 fragility' datapoint, not a censorship-action proper. needs_check on the exact 2024-05 date and attacker attribution.

candidates.title: Tornado Cash project integrates Chainalysis Oracle to block OFAC-sanctioned addresses from dapp (pre-OFAC self-censorship)
candidates.rationale: Tornado Cash team voluntarily integrated Chainalysis Oracle into tornado.cash dapp 2022-04-15 (four months before the 2022-08-08 OFAC SDN designation) to block OFAC-sanctioned wallets from the user-facing dapp — but explicitly NOT at the smart-contract layer. Codes the rare 'frontend-only voluntary self-censorship' subtype: a privacy-tool operator preemptively complying with US sanctions via its UI while leaving protocol functions unrestricted. Predates the OFAC designation, the 2022-08 frontend cascade, and the 2023 storm-semenov-doj-2023 indictment; useful as the earliest data point in the Tornado Cash event family. Useful for the paper's claim that frontend/protocol decoupling appeared *voluntarily* before the OFAC trigger.

candidates.title: ConsenSys MetaMask Snaps launches with regional/jurisdictional restrictions on third-party plugins
candidates.rationale: MetaMask Snaps (third-party plugin system) launched September 2023 with operator-level region/jurisdiction controls on which Snaps users can install. Not a single trigger date / single block, but a structural change to the wallet plugin ecosystem with implications for L3/L4 censorship at the wallet-plugin substrate. P2 because the censorship action is a class-level policy rather than a concrete dated block; needs_check on exact launch date and on whether the regional restrictions were enforced in the September 2023 launch or added later. Included for completeness of the wallet/plugin substrate.
